# The proposal
<!--
How are you going to solve the problem? Include the concrete actions you
will take and an estimated timeline. What are likely failure modes and
how will you recover from them?

This is where the proposal should be outlined.
-->

This project aims to provide algorithms around the following concepts:

- binary construction

- likert construction

- likert conversion

- vector description

- weight construction

## Overview
<!--
At a high-level address what your proposal is and how it will address
the problem identified. Highlight any benefits to the R Community that
follow from solving the problem. This should be your most compelling
section.

Include concrete actions you will take and estimated timeline.
-->

The proposal is to create and submit an R package dealing with likert-type data conversions to different formats.

## Detail
<!--
Go into more detail about the specifics of the project and how it delivers
against the problem.

Depending on project type the detail section should include:
-->

### Minimum Viable Product

<!--
What is the smallest thing you can build that delivers value to your users?
-->
The minimum goals is to have a lightweight R package hosted on GitHub that successfully executes bi-directional transliteration between raw character vectors and structured ordinal Likert scales, focusing on likert construction and likert conversion modules.

### Architecture

<!--
What does the high-level architecture look like?
-->
The package will be built within the R statistical computing ecosystem with minimal external dependencies. It will feature an optimized core chunking engine designed to pass integration tests with local memory backends. The internal logic will revolve around transliteration and dynamic conversion algorithms around the main concepts and function of this project.

### Assumptions

<!--
What assumptions are you making that, if proven false, would invalidate the project?
-->
There is high expectation that the project would be delivered with no particular risk associated with all timelines, except emergencies or natural disasters, like COVID-19 happens.

### External dependencies

<!--
What external dependencies does the project have (e.g. libraries, services, other projects, etc.)?
-->
The proposed package would have minimum dependencies but would rely of `tidyverse` established routines and workflows.
